solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Painting of model's footwear (detail)

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped model a shoemaker works on; with the possessive S
the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole

explanation.surface: A cobbler's dummy foot and its shoe are given a close look, as if in a detailed painting.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAST is a cobbler's wooden model of a foot, so 'model's' gives LASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's famous mural of Christ's final meal is one of the best-known paintings in the world.

clue.text: Beach hero bringing 50 to the surface

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the surface, so the letter is brought up to the start

parts.note: a hero is someone idolised, an idol
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A lifeguard-type hero hauls fifty people up out of the sea onto the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing ... to the surface' moves L from the end of IDOL to the top of this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public bathing place or beach resort, from the Venice Lido.

clue.text: Make confession to admit one's acting alone

definitions.note: read as 'one who is acting alone'

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
to let on is to admit or reveal

explanation.surface: A suspect confesses to the police that they committed the crime without accomplices.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an individual on their own, one who operates singly rather than in a pair or group.

clue.text: Abandon abrasive cleaner

definitions.meaning: to ... a plan is to cancel or drop it
a gritty cream for cleansing skin

explanation.surface: Someone gives up on a harsh scouring product.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapping a plan and a gritty exfoliating cream are both senses of the same everyday word.

clue.text: Get sportsman treatment

parts.note: a pro is a professional sportsman
a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: An injured athlete seeks to get physiotherapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to obtain or acquire it.

clue.text: Passed type of Jag with pedals spinning

parts.note: the E-type is a classic Jaguar sports car

indicators.note: the pedals go round, so their letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An E-type Jaguar sped past with its pedals whirling.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PEDALS from 'spinning' is LAPSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has gone by, slipped past.

clue.text: Favourite's backed for pace

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a pet is a favourite; with the possessive S

explanation.surface: The favourite in a race has been backed by punters for its speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like betting talk but turns PETS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace in walking.

clue.text: Taste grappling with sound

indicators.note: the taste grips the abbreviation for with in its arms, holding it inside

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

explanation.surface: Someone tackles flavour and noise together, as in a tasting of wine with music.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a ringing nasal sound, like a plucked string.

clue.text: Promotion describing grapes post-treading?

definitions.meaning: advancement to a higher office or rank
trodden grapes are mashed but not yet fermenting

explanation.surface: A wine-maker's step up the ladder is marked by the state of the trodden harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as PRE-FERMENT, the stage after treading and before fermentation.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferment is a formal word for promotion to a higher post, especially in the Church.

clue.text: Fast food that's cooked right

parts.note: food that is cooked is done

explanation.surface: A takeaway that has been cooked properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A doner kebab is a staple of takeaway shops.

clue.text: Drink over limit, getting regularly addled

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a range is the extent or limit of something

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Someone drinks over the limit and ends up befuddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with oranges.

clue.text: Supreme in the year of our lord, our Father's creator?

parts.note: grand means first-rate, supreme

parts.words: in the year of our lord
parts.note: AD stands for Anno Domini, Latin for in the year of our Lord

explanation.surface: A religious phrase about the supreme Lord and the Father who created all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our Father' looks like God; it is just someone's dad, whose father made him.
explanation.definitionFit: A father's own father is the grandfather of the speaker, so in a sense he brought their father into being.

clue.text: What 'ard-working scientist puts in perhaps works

indicators.note: the dropped H of ''ard' signals that the letter H is dropped here too

parts.note: the time a scientist works is lab hours

explanation.surface: A question about what a diligent researcher contributes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What ... puts in' is the time spent in a lab; said with a dropped H, as in ''ard', the phrase becomes LAB 'OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour is to work hard, so labours means works or toils.

clue.text: Old German viewpoint

definitions.meaning: the ... were an ancient Germanic people who settled England

explanation.surface: An old German's way of seeing things.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the early Germanic tribe, and a slant or perspective, share the same spelling.

clue.text: Deviously prime agent to infiltrate

indicators.note: deviously means by twisting routes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spymaster cunningly prepares an agent to penetrate an enemy organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To impregnate is to soak through or permeate, so it can mean to infiltrate or pervade.

clue.text: What arises in marsh where royal one encounters Macbeth?

parts.note: one, as a royal speaker refers to himself, is me
Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor

explanation.surface: A query about a Scottish moorland where a king meets the murderous Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encounters' joins the two pieces. A thane was a Scottish lord, Macbeth's title before he became king.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas is the common name for the gas that bubbles up from rotting vegetation in swamps.

clue.text: I don't believe where armed robber was seen!

definitions.meaning: what an unbeliever in God says
an armed robber would be seen at a heist

explanation.surface: An incredulous witness reacts to news of where a gunman was spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as AT HEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without faith in any god would declare that they do not believe.

clue.text: Movement to keep platform in check

indicators.note: the barrier holds the platform within it

parts.note: a dam checks the flow of water
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A political movement wants to keep a stage under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Dadaism was an anarchic early-20th-century art movement.

clue.text: I find in the end dubious nite clubs mainly all the same

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word find is used
dubious signals the letters are in a doubtful, jumbled order

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone finds that dodgy nightclubs are all much alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' makes ENTIC from NITE plus C; 'mainly' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are identical are exactly alike in every respect.

clue.text: Cowboy managed singer

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: A cowboy acted as manager for a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy who owns or works a cattle ranch can be called by that title.

clue.text: One cut off from the world tweaks crossword, perhaps reversing ending

definitions.text: One cut off from the world

indicators.note: only the final pair of letters is turned round

parts.note: to rewrite a puzzle's clues is to re-clue it

explanation.surface: A hermit amuses himself by fiddling with a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing ending' turns the closing ES round to SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is a hermit who lives apart from society.

clue.text: Grounded without right to go out, producing resentment

indicators.note: the letters go out of their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenager grounded and denied the right to go out feels aggrieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes R away from GROUNDED; 'to go out' then rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offence or indignation, as in 'in high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Maybe snare young fox and beat keeper

parts.note: a snare is an example of a drum
a kit is a young fox

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper might set a snare for a fox cub and beat the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer's set of drums keeps time, holding the rhythm for the band.

clue.text: Fashion house received English cricketer informally

indicators.note: received as heard, in the ear rather than on the page

parts.note: Graham Gooch, an England captain, given a pet name

explanation.surface: A fashion house welcomed an England cricketer to a casual event.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Gooch was an England batsman and captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Gucci is an Italian luxury fashion label.

clue.text: Works on ship sailing circuit, it's said

indicators.note: a signal that the word is to be spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a cruise is a round voyage by ship

explanation.surface: A sailor works aboard a ship on a round-trip voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To crew is to serve as a member of a ship's company.

clue.text: 'What's for tea?' Politician cracks open bottle

indicators.note: the politician breaks into the bottle and sits inside

parts.note: a cruet is a small bottle for oil or vinegar
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: At teatime a politician opens a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a British griddle bun, toasted and buttered at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted bun eaten with butter is a classic item served at British afternoon tea.

clue.text: Set down unfinished pasta

indicators.note: the final letter is left off

parts.note: to set something down in writing is to have penned it

explanation.surface: Someone puts down a half-eaten plate of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Penne is pasta in short tubes cut on the slant.

clue.text: It's more suitable when not teetotal at heart

definitions.text: It's more suitable when not teetotal at heart

indicators.note: the abstainer's letters are not there, so they are removed
the letters taken out are in the middle of the word

parts.note: better means more suitable

explanation.surface: A drinker's view that the stuff is preferable when you're no abstainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: to a non-abstainer this drink is the better choice.
explanation.definitionFit: The ale or lager a non-abstainer prefers is exactly what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Amazed at rugby players winning three points

indicators.note: the pieces win, or gain, the points inside them

parts.note: W, E and S are compass points
a ruck is a group of rugby forwards contesting the ball

explanation.surface: Spectators amazed at rugby players who win with a three-point penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three points' looks like a penalty goal in rugby; it is three compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awestruck is filled with wonder, overwhelmed and astonished.

clue.text: Macaroni cheese holding interest for minority

indicators.note: the dish holds the letters within its words

explanation.surface: Macaroni cheese has a specialised appeal for only a few people.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche interest is a specialised one appealing to a small group.

clue.text: Formerly Queen Street

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A road once called Queen Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic word meaning once or in the past, as in erstwhile.

clue.text: One ringing round sets out to create a hit

indicators.note: the bell-ringer goes round the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: someone who rings a bell, a beller

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer goes round setting out to make a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a peal of bells; it signals one piece wrapping the other, and 'to create' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A best-seller is a book or record that sells in huge numbers, a commercial success.
